gen-gf-phudu-fs-familjen-grotesk: Familjen Grotesk is a lively plain sans with bowls left open on one side and lowercase that stands tall against its capitals. Phudu's outline holds one steady, unshaded line, and that contrast is the hook.
gen-gf-phudu-fs-hind: Bold and distinctive, Phudu draws every curve with generous openings and a plain, pen-like line. Hind sits next to it quietly, its lowercase nearly matching the capitals, so the two feel like a shout and a nod.
gen-gf-phudu-fs-nunito: Nunito reads soft and approachable, with big round bowls and terminals that finish clear of the stem. Phudu is the opposite, constant-lined like blueprint lettering, and it would feel cramped if shrunk down to body size.
gen-gf-phudu-fs-pilcrow-rounded: Chunky, confident shapes up top and open, tall-lowercase warmth below. Phudu is best at making a loud, distinctive entrance, and Pilcrow Rounded is best at curves that refuse to close and letters packed with thin gaps.
gen-gf-phudu-fs-quicksand: Quicksand reads like a row of blown glass bulbs, tall in the lowercase and approachable, with terminals finishing well clear of the stem. Phudu is the bold one here, so let this body type stay modest in size.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-actor: Actor reads clean and modern, its wide s curves barely curled in. Phudu brings a single-width stroke in every glyph and a loud personality, while Actor stays low-key beside it, a quiet foil to a showy partner.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-akatab: Akatab has round letters that look cupped rather than clenched. Phudu's stroke weight never varies, and that rigid, bold outline against Akatab's easygoing softness is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-alan-sans: Alan Sans reads modern and businesslike, with curve tails held well back. Phudu keeps its thickness fixed around every bend, so the two feel like a loud announcement followed by a measured reply.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-albert-sans: Albert Sans is a contemporary sans-serif whose apertures stay open at tiny sizes and whose stroke thickness ignores direction. Phudu supplies the bold, distinctive headline voice, and Albert Sans quietly handles everything after it.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-alef: Phudu's strokes look like hollow pipes, bold and unmistakable, with generous openings at every curve. Alef takes over for the longer read, its open-ended curves keeping a modern, clean rhythm going line after line.
